chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us, from al-Qasim b. Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan b. Rashid, from Abu 'Abdullah al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me on his pulpit:

O Ali! Allah (mighty and majestic) has gifted you with the love of the needy and the oppressed on earth, so you were pleased with them as brethren and they were pleased with you as an Imam. Blessed is he who loves you and believes in you, and woe to he who hates you and belies you. O Ali! You are the banner of this nation; whoever loves you succeeds, and whoever hates you perishes. O Ali! I am the City of Knowledge and you are its gate - can a city be entered except through its gate?! O Ali! The people of your love are every penitent, mindful person, and every humble one who, if he swore upon Allah, would have his oath fulfilled. O Ali! Your brethren are every pure, devout striver who loves for your sake and hates for your sake - despised among creation but great in rank with Allah. O Ali! Those who love you are the neighbors of Allah in the Abode of Paradise; they do not grieve for what they left behind. O Ali! I am the guardian of whoever you befriend, and I am the enemy of whoever you oppose. O Ali! Whoever loves you has loved me, and whoever hates you has hated me. O Ali! Your brethren have withered lips; monasticism is recognized in their faces. O Ali! Your brethren rejoice in three stations: at the departure of their souls while I and you witness them, at the questioning in their graves, and at the Great Presentation and at the Bridge when creation is asked about their faith and they cannot answer.

O Ali! Your war is my war, and your peace is my peace; and my war is the war of Allah. O Ali! Give glad tidings to your brethren, for Allah is pleased with them. O Ali! You are the Commander of the Faithful and the Leader of the Radiant Ones. O Ali! Your Shi'a are the chosen ones. Were it not for you and your Shi'a, no religion would be established for Allah, and were it not for your presence on earth, no rain would fall from the sky. O Ali! You have a treasure in Paradise. O Ali! You and your Shi'a are the establishers of justice. O Ali! You and your Shi'a will be at the Pond. Regarding you was this verse revealed: 'Surely those for whom the finest reward has preceded from Us - those will be kept far from it' [21:101], and 'The Great Dismay will not grieve them' [21:103].

O Ali! You and your Shi'a will be sought at the Standing, while you will be in the Gardens enjoying bliss. O Ali! The angels and the treasurers long for you. O Ali! Your Shi'a are those who fear Allah in secret. O Ali! Your Shi'a are those who compete for the highest ranks. O Ali! The deeds of your Shi'a will be presented to me every Friday. O Ali! Your mention is in the Torah, and likewise in the Gospel. So ask the people of the Gospel about Ilya. O Ali! The mention of your companions in heaven is greater than on earth.

O Ali! The spirits of your Shi'a ascend to heaven during their sleep and at their death. O Ali! Tell your companions to abstain from the deeds that their enemy commits. O Ali! The anger of Allah is intensified against those who despise them and dissociate from you, and hate us the People of the House. O Ali! Convey my greetings to those whom I will not see. Inform them that Allah is pleased with them and that He commands the angels to seek forgiveness on their behalf.

O Ali! Do not cease supporting a people who love you out of my love for you. They have borne hostility yet refused anything but our support - so be merciful to them, for Allah has chosen them for our sake, created them from our clay, and entrusted them with our secret. While the people are lost in misguidance, your Shi'a are on the upright path of truth. The world is not of them and they are not of it. Those are the lanterns in the darkness. Those are the lanterns in the darkness. Those are the lanterns in the darkness.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful - the exclusive title of Imam Ali
key_terms.المساكين والمستضعفين: The needy and the oppressed - those marginalized by society
key_terms.حزب الله: Party of Allah - Quranic designation (5:56) for the allies of God
key_terms.مدينة العلم: City of Knowledge - title for the Prophet as the source of divine knowledge
key_terms.مصابيح الدجى: Lanterns in the darkness - metaphor for the Shi'a guiding in times of misguidance

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Imam Ali and his followers in the Sermon of the Pulpit?
ai.summary: In this lengthy sermon delivered from his pulpit, the Prophet Muhammad (s) addresses Imam Ali (as) with a series of declarations praising him and his followers (Shi'a). The sermon was narrated through a chain going back to Imam al-Sadiq (as). The Prophet describes Ali as the banner of the nation, the gate of the City of Knowledge, the Commander of the Faithful, and the leader of the shining believers. He characterizes Ali's followers as chosen ones whose mention appears in the Torah and the Gospel, whose spirits are received by the angels, and who will be safe on the Day of Judgment at the Pond and under the shade of the Throne. The Prophet cites Quran 21:101 and 21:103 as having been revealed about them. He commands Ali to convey his greetings to future believers, urges them to hold fast to the rope of Allah, and concludes by calling them 'the lanterns in the darkness' - repeated three times for emphasis.
